meta.homeDescription: A self-hosted webhook inbox and notification router for media servers and the services around them.
meta.releasesDescription: Bilingual release notes for Seshat Beta and Release channels.

home.headline: Every event, made legible.
home.lead: Seshat turns noisy webhook payloads into a clear event stream, then routes the right message to the right channel—on your infrastructure.
home.mockBody: Artwork, episode context, playback details and provider links—without digging through raw JSON.
home.principlesTitle: A calm control plane for busy services.
home.principlesLead: Keep protocols isolated, delivery observable and every event useful to a human.
home.featureInboxBody: Filter by app and message type, inspect normalized data, and page through history without loading everything at once.
home.featureAppsBody: Jellyfin and Emby remain the source of truth, with TMDB as a focused metadata fallback.
home.featureRoutingBody: Generate structured content once, then let each notification channel choose plain text or Markdown.
home.featureDeliveryBody: Bounded retries, clear channel diagnostics and business logs keep failures understandable.
home.ecosystemTitle: Connect media events to the channels your team already watches.
home.deployBody: Run the unified Seshat container with SQLite by default, or connect PostgreSQL when your deployment grows.
home.copyHint: Pin an immutable version tag for production deployments.
home.versionTitle: Choose the pace that fits your deployment.
home.betaBody: Early access to the newest integrated changes.
home.releaseBody: The stable lane for production environments.
home.footer: Open source, self-hosted, and designed for understandable operations.

releases.title: What changed, in your language.
releases.lead: Beta and Release histories stay independent. Your installation only checks the lane it is running.
releases.betaDescription: Preview builds and the newest integrated features.
releases.releaseDescription: Stable builds intended for production use.
